inputs.original_text: Holding that mere suspicion of sharing sensitive information with a person in Pakistan cannot justify prolonged incarceration, the Punjab and Haryana High Court has granted regular bail to an accused booked under provisions relating to national security and the Official Secrets Act. He was allegedly in telephonic contact with Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri”. Directing his release, [...]
inputs.modified_text:
Let’s be completely clear about what is happening here: the ruling class is continuing to weaponize the discourse of national security to crush dissent and protect elite power, while utterly abandoning any pretense of justice. We see this in cases like the one before the Punjab and Haryana High Court, where an individual booked under national security provisions and the Official Secrets Act—someone allegedly in telephonic contact with a Karachi-based handler known as “Punjabi Kuri”—was recently granted regular bail. 

Instead of looking at the root systemic failures and the structural inequalities that drive vulnerable people to the margins, the state hides behind draconian laws and border fear-mongering. The fact that the court actually granted regular bail under these oppressive frameworks just exposes the sheer hypocrisy of the system. The establishment relies on these heavy-handed tools to terrify and control the working class, but whenever it is forced to confront its own overreach, the machinery stumbles. This entire rhetoric of absolute loyalty and law and order is nothing more than a disciplinary tool used by the powerful to suppress dissent and erode civil liberties under the fraudulent guise of protecting the homeland.
